description: Development release history preserved off the game menu. Append every future release here until the 1.0 Version History page is built.

entries.title: LIVING NPC ROUTINES AND PHYSICAL INTERACTIONS
entries.notes: Existing Haven recruits and four articulated faction-story contacts now follow deterministic, accelerated work/patrol/rest cycles using the live character rig, with walking speed feeding the actual limb animation. The actors turn toward nearby players and stop to face them during conversations. Actual player and enemy gunshots trigger a bounded alarm reaction within hearing distance; vendor actors stay behind their stalls but turn for conversations and duck at danger. New live body colliders keep the player from passing through these actors, and NPC movement checks world props, constructed settlement structures, nearby residents and the player. Named story contacts remain reachable either at their original terminal or by approaching their physical model. Position, heading, work phase and alert state persist in a new isolated saved record with strict distance limits; old quest, inventory, faction, settlement and vendor saves are not rewritten. This pass is a short testing-field work/rest simulation, not a full day/night schedule or a companion AI; keep that distinction clear. All release notes stay off the homepage until the dedicated 1.0 archive page.

entries.title: NPC DIALOGUE AND MERCHANT CHARISMA NEGOTIATION
entries.notes: Physical story contacts and all six merchants now open a focused conversation overlay that keeps the live 3D world visible. Dialogues offer numbered replies, accessible keyboard shortcuts and optional pages for seven or more possible quest responses; no existing mission branch, faction reputation change, XP reward or saved quest outcome was removed. Merchants have individual greetings, supply explanations and a one-attempt Charisma 6 negotiation. A successful check grants 8% better buying and selling rates for one confirmed barter only, applied consistently to unit quotes, staged offers, wallet/carry previews and the actual atomic transaction. Trade access is still controlled by saved faction reputation, and negotiated rates do not survive leaving the merchant. The homepage remains concise and this entry is archived for the future 1.0 history screen.

entries.title: POWER ARMOR SIX-PLATE CONFIGURATION OVERHAUL
entries.notes: Improved the existing six-slot interactive power-armor service terminal with a detailed chassis schematic that can be clicked or operated with keyboard controls. Each slot displays its live durability and visually distinguishes salvaged T-45, T-60, and prototype T-01 armor when healthy, along with critical and missing/broken plates. Selecting an owned replacement previews its exact effective armor-point change, current-to-new durability and condition before the player confirms installation or removal; broken plates correctly show zero protection until repaired. Repair components now have individual sourced ledgers for pouch stock, settlement storage and automatic junk breakdown, with shortages identified before any transaction. All existing frame-specific saved pieces, core behavior, guarded equip/removal actions and transactional repairs remain intact. The homepage stays concise; history is retained for the planned 1.0 version page.

entries.title: WEAPON WORKBENCH INSPECTION OVERHAUL
entries.notes: Reworked the physical Haven firearm workbench presentation without changing the tested crafting rules. Compatible assemblies can now be filtered between all parts, ready-to-craft replacements, already-owned parts and recipes with missing materials. The selected-part panel shows actual current-to-preview firearm changes with separate improvement and drawback colors, and a per-component resource ledger distinguishing carried stock, settlement storage and materials that automatic junk scrapping would recover. Recipes clearly identify shortages and show exactly which stored junk objects would be consumed, but no resources are touched until the user confirms crafting. Installed and previously crafted parts can still be selected free, owned weapons and their saves are preserved, and the homepage remains uncluttered with release history reserved for the 1.0 archive page.

entries.title: VENDOR TRADING TERMINAL OVERHAUL
entries.notes: Rebuilt merchant presentation around searchable BUY and SELL lists with independent category filters and real item inspections. Equipment comparisons show actual firearm damage and reload/magazine values, equipped armor protection deltas, aid effects, power-armor durability, junk breakdowns and accurate unit prices. Every merchant now has a finite, saved caps balance, displayed beside your wallet and enforced by the existing transactional barter preview; buying can fund selling in the same confirmed offer, but a vendor cannot pay more caps than they own. Old vendor stock and character saves migrate without losing equipment or stock. The homepage stays concise, with all development notes archived for a single Version History page at 1.0.

entries.title: CHARACTER TERMINAL OVERHAUL
entries.notes: Inventory now supports live item search, sorting by name/value/weight, keyboard-accessible item inspection, actual weapon and armor figures, equip state, scrap yields and carry totals. STATUS displays current SPECIAL attributes, level progress, unspent points, radiation HP limit, and AP alongside the real six-zone armor display; the perks screen opens directly from it. Quest journal filters separate active and completed history without changing tracking. The existing fog-of-war map has a discovered-destinations list with working waypoint controls and quick return to STATUS, ITEMS or QUESTS. Existing equipment, exploration, quest progress, and save data are preserved.

entries.title: PHYSICAL JUNK & WORKSHOP SCRAPPING
entries.notes: Eight real junk inventory objects now have individual weight, sale prices and exact crafting-component yields, including desk fans, typewriters, alarm clocks and adhesive tape. Raiders can drop salvage objects, and WREN sells finite stock. At Haven Junction, open Inventory → Junk to deposit your junk in the saved workshop stash, retrieve it, scrap one or all copies, and withdraw stored components. Stored items no longer contribute to your carried weight. Weapon and optics benches, local settlement construction and power-armor repairs automatically break down only the stored junk needed for their exact material recipes. Every crafting attempt is transactional: an impossible or failed craft leaves junk, components, caps and equipment unchanged, while successful work saves unused byproducts for later projects. Older inventories and settlement saves continue to load.

entries.title: FOOD, WATER & CHEM EFFECTS
entries.notes: DOC VALE now sells six functional supplies: purified water, trail stew, contaminated water, a combat stimulant, focus tonic and Rad Shield. Food and drinks heal actual HP while contaminated supplies add real, persistent radiation that reduces your HP cap. The three chems temporarily improve actual weapon damage, the live V.A.T.S. chance calculation, or radiation protection; they do not stack with themselves. Active timers and their durations persist across save/reload, pause while in menus and clear on death. The status screen and both field/power-armor HUDs show active bonuses. Existing medkits still treat real limb injuries and Radiation Flush still removes accumulated rads without healing damage.

entries.title: REAL CARRY WEIGHT & ENCUMBRANCE
entries.notes: Replaced the artificial 30-slot backpack cap with real per-item weight, including weapons, armor, supplies, spare power-armor plates and all 31 crafting components. Normal-mode ammunition weighs nothing. Carry allowance is 200 + 10 per Strength point, with a functional field backpack bonus and effective Strength 11 while wearing a power-armor frame. Taking loot and buying goods can put you over the allowance without destroying or blocking items. Overencumbered players walk slowly, cannot sprint or jump, and consume the actual shared AP meter while moving. Inventory, loot, vendors, field HUD and power visor all show the same live weight and overload status. Old inventory saves still load without losing entries.

entries.title: LIVE V.A.T.S. TARGET SCANNER
entries.notes: Real animated enemies now have a world-tracked targeting frame, six body-part probability markers, live health bar, range and crippled-limb status. The selected part glows amber and queued targets are marked on the battlefield. Markers use projected, visible physical hitboxes and disappear when obscured. Combat, NPC AI, movement and weapon timing continue in real time for multiplayer. The XP required for every new level is also 50% higher (level 1 now takes 255 XP, up from 170), without changing saved levels, earned progress or perks.

entries.title: S.P.E.C.I.A.L. PERK INTEGRATION
entries.notes: All seven attributes now affect the live sandbox: Strength adds backpack slots alongside recoil control; Perception improves targeting; Endurance supports survival; Charisma changes real buy/sell prices; Intelligence controls XP and workbench material discounts; Agility reduces V.A.T.S. shot AP alongside movement bonuses; and Luck speeds V.A.T.S. critical-meter charging. Silver Tongue adds a barter advantage, Ghost Runner reduces V.A.T.S. AP costs, and Resourceful discounts both weapon assemblies and optics. Vendor cart totals and workbench recipes match the actual transaction, while existing saves and already crafted parts remain intact. Open S.P.E.C.I.A.L. with L.

entries.title: CRIPPLED LIMBS AFFECT ENEMY COMBAT
entries.notes: Shooting a Raider's legs now causes real movement penalties and an asymmetric limp. Arm, head and chest injuries lower their actual hit probability; all six body-part conditions are tracked until the enemy dies or the arena is reset. Your own injured legs now visibly affect third-person gait and subtly change first-person walking motion. V.A.T.S. identifies crippled limbs. Heal your injuries with real medical supplies; resetting enemies clears only their injuries.

entries.title: LIVE V.A.T.S. SHOT QUEUE
entries.notes: Press T to enter tactical targeting without slowing the world. Use Tab to cycle visible hostiles and 1–6 to select body parts, then left-click to queue shots within your available AP and ammunition. Enter executes the queue as real weapon shots over time; Backspace removes the last shot. Space reserves one charged critical for a queued shot. AI, movement and incoming fire continue normally, and moving behind cover can invalidate a queued shot.

entries.title: TACTICAL BODY-PART TARGETING
entries.notes: Original real-time target selection added six limb hit percentages based on distance, cover, Perception and injuries; real ammo, weapon cooldown, shared stamina/AP and a hit-earned critical meter. T or Escape exits tactical targeting.

entries.title: LIMB INJURIES & FUNCTIONAL MEDICAL CARE
entries.notes: Incoming hits now damage the specific struck head, torso, arm or leg. A crippled leg actually reduces movement speed; two crippled legs prevent sprinting; arm and head injuries worsen aim, arm injuries add recoil and chest wounds raise stamina drain. Field and power-armor injury warnings and the inventory's negative-effects page display the physical condition. Real Field Medkits treat the most damaged limb and restore up to 40 HP; they remain usable for an injury when HP is full, consume exactly one item and never repair every limb for free. All six limb conditions save between sessions and are reset on respawn and deliberate combat-test restart. Existing save games migrate with healthy limbs.

entries.title: LIVE SIX-LEVEL RADIATION GAUGE
entries.notes: The RAD needle and number now read live exposure intensity on a zero-to-six scale instead of slowly accumulated lifetime radiation dose. Zero means safe; approaching the actual waste site increases the level through one to six. An occupied, intact power-armor suit reduces the measured intensity. Both power-armor and ordinary field displays immediately react when you enter, move within, and leave a radioactive area, including when no further dose accrues. The separate accumulated RADS total remains visible for health-cap and medicine tracking.

entries.title: ACTUAL RADIATION HP LOSS & HUD FIX
entries.notes: Radiation now hurts real current HP even when the player was already wounded, in addition to limiting maximum survivable health. Both ordinary HP bars and the power-armor HP dial use the full 100-HP scale, so dropping to 75 HP visibly shows 75% rather than a deceptively full 75/75 bar. The unusable health portion is marked red on both ordinary bars; the separate RAD gauge and counter continue showing accumulated rads. Radiation can cause a real death and trigger the first-person death sequence. Radiation Flush removes radiation and restores the health cap but does not heal missing HP.

entries.title: HAZARD SCENE REPAIR & COLLISION PASS
entries.notes: Moved the radiation source entirely clear of the raised training ramp. Replaced the billboard and buried miniature drums with a ground-level waste depot: rusted full-size ribbed drums, warning decals, an overturned tank, bent metal fence, irregular leaking pools and debris. Solid debris now blocks bullets and movement. The massive solid-green slope is now a textured weathered-concrete ramp with visible slab joints. Radiation intensity and medical treatment remain unchanged. This is still a testing field, not a finished campaign location.

entries.title: RADIATION & FULL RPG REBUILD FOUNDATION
entries.notes: Radiation is no longer a fake zeroed-out power-armor gauge. A visible, physically located contaminated drum spill on the east side of the field now applies persistent radiation over time, reduces your real maximum HP, and appears on both the regular HUD and power armor's live dial. An occupied power frame reduces exposure. DOC VALE sells Radiation Flush medical treatment, which removes rads without magically restoring lost HP; use a medkit separately to heal. Radiation survives reloads and respawn, with bounded save migration. The full-game redesign standards, current gaps and phased acceptance tests are now documented in WASTELAND_DESIGN_BIBLE.md.

entries.title: MODULAR ROOF MODELS & SCALE FIX
entries.notes: Roofs now share the exact 3×3-metre footprint of timber foundations and fit above 2.7-metre walls. The corrugated flat roof has individual scavenged sheet-metal panels, seams and visible framing; a new gabled scrap roof uses two physically slanted panels, a ridge cap and rafters. With grid snap enabled, roofs center on foundation bays or the bay adjoining an actual wall edge, never on top of the wall itself. The preview calls out ROOF BAY SNAPPED. Roofs require a properly aligned supporting wall, and storing or scrapping that wall is blocked until its roof is safely removed.

entries.title: WALL CORNER JOINING & EDGE SNAP
entries.notes: Walls and doorframes can now meet at proper ninety-degree corners and T-junctions without being rejected as overlapping structures. With grid snap enabled, a wall near an existing wall endpoint or foundation edge automatically aligns into place, and the preview reports CORNER SNAPPED. True collisions with rocks, other props and crossed walls still block construction. The previous duplicate collision check for placed structures is removed, so valid joins survive saving and reloading.

entries.title: REAL SETTLEMENT OBJECT STORAGE
entries.notes: F no longer gives components back. It puts a complete player-built object into workshop storage and adds a (1), (2) and so on beside that object in the construction menu. Choose its blueprint and place the stored copy without spending materials; the count decreases when placed, even after reloading. X remains the scrap key for both pre-existing settlement objects and your own structures, permanently removing them for salvaged materials. Storing and scrapping never create duplicate supplies, and existing saves migrate with empty storage.

entries.title: TRUE SETTLEMENT SCRAP & POWER ARMOR GANTRY
entries.notes: X now permanently scraps junk, old settlement fixtures, or any player-built structure for actual recovered materials; F stores your placed structures for a full construction-material refund. The original Haven weapon bench and the individual floor, walls and roof of a derelict shack are editable scrap targets, with every removal saved. The unnecessary salvage sorting table is no longer offered as a new blueprint, but already-placed ones remain recoverable. Power armor service racks now have an open yellow A-frame, overhead hoist, hydraulic arms, bracing and safety markings in the style of a wasteland maintenance gantry.

entries.title: PLACEABLE WORKBENCHES & WORLD SALVAGE
entries.notes: A new WORKSHOPS category provides a physical weapon-modification bench, a power-armor service rack (bring a real frame nearby) and a salvage sorting table. Built weapon benches can now modify guns with E, the same as Haven's original fixed bench—there is still no U remote shortcut. Haven also has distinctive abandoned junk that can be scrapped permanently in building mode: aim at a piece and press X to turn it into actual wood, steel, copper, circuitry and other parts. Salvaged clutter disappears from the world and stays gone across reloads; each object pays out only once. Player-built structures still store for a full material refund.

entries.title: LIVING SETTLEMENT WORKSHOP
entries.notes: A dedicated settlement-testing entry and eight build categories replace the single flat list. Press Tab to switch categories, 1–7 to choose pieces, and B to exit. Your gun and gun UI disappear while building and return when you leave. Crops, pumps, purifiers, beds, guard posts, sentry turrets, generators, lamps, storage and a powered recruitment beacon now have distinctive 3D models and real materials costs. The top dashboard tracks residents, food, water, electricity demand, defense, beds and changing happiness; recruiting a settler requires enough powered beacon capacity, food, water and sleeping space.

entries.title: HAVEN JUNCTION WORKSHOP BUILDING
entries.notes: Enter Haven by the foreman and weapon bench, then press B to build. Choose one of seven original scavenged structures, see a green or red world-space preview, rotate or turn off grid snapping, and place pieces only when you own the wood, steel, cloth and other required components. Buildings block movement and gunfire where solid, persist across reloads, and can be stored by aiming and pressing X (or undoing the last with Z) for a full material refund. Roofs need walls or doorframes nearby. This is the construction foundation; settler jobs, electrical wiring, crops and water production are future systems.

entries.title: CORRECT CORNER PEEK DIRECTION
entries.notes: Guards now choose left or right based on their facing and the actual firing lane. A corner peek holds one shoulder until the peek finishes, preventing the character from leaning the other way halfway through. Automatic cover leaning clears its old direction whenever an explicit corner peek begins.

entries.title: RAISED RIFLES & PHYSICAL CORNER PEEKING
entries.notes: NPC eyes now follow the animated head rather than an invisible chest-height point. When a rock exposes only the player's head, raiders lift their actual rifle and aim from its real muzzle. Around corners they turn and lean their rendered torso, head and held gun, with both hands gripping the rifle; a shoulder peek only counts when the projectile path is truly clear. Existing cover routes, ammunition and reloading still govern attacks.

entries.title: ENEMY INTELLIGENCE & COMBAT OVERHAUL
entries.notes: Guards no longer fire sideways before facing their target or draw every missed shot far ahead of someone standing still. Steady observation improves accuracy without granting perfect aim; moving targets, recoil, distance and suppression still matter. Scouts, raiders and enforcers now navigate around blocking cover, commit to firing lanes between flanks, retain a short aim memory on brief occlusions, and use smoother speed-based steps, strafing lean, search glances, reloads and hit reactions.

entries.title: FIRST-PERSON DEATH CINEMATIC
entries.notes: On fatal damage your view staggers down to your knees, pauses, then pitches into the ground with a brief impact jolt. Only after the fall fades out does YOU DIED appear. The Haven respawn and recoverable power-armor frame are unchanged.

entries.title: DEATH & POWER ARMOR RECOVERY
entries.notes: Fatal damage now plays a third-person collapse before showing a death screen. Respawn at Haven with your backpack, progression and world changes intact. A power-armor frame stays where you fell. The map shows only your most recently worn parked frame, and you may track or untrack it without replacing your own waypoint.

entries.title: SETTLEMENT WEAPON WORKBENCH
entries.notes: Weapon modifications require physically walking to Haven's workshop bench and pressing E nearby. The U shortcut and remote-workbench menu button are gone; the firing lane no longer contains a weapon workbench.

entries.title: READ-ONLY DIAGNOSTICS
entries.notes: F3 reveals performance and gameplay status without a keybind cheat sheet. Free healing, enemy resetting/freezing, station teleporting and dummy-armor editing are no longer accessible to players. Quick-jump buttons to the combat arena, trading row and power-armor frame have been removed. Find frames in the world and use ordinary gameplay controls instead. Both compasses remain visible.

entries.title: FACTION POWER ARMOR & FOUND FRAMES
entries.notes: Power armor only comes from visibly armored combatants, trusted Iron Dominion/Rust Vultures quartermasters, or abandoned powered chassis. Earn 35 faction reputation to trade their T-45 parts and fusion cores, or 65 for advanced T-60 parts; formal membership is not required. Enforcers and raiders may wear armor in combat. Three incomplete, damaged T-45 frames with cores can be discovered and configured in the testing field. Each frame's parts, core and location save independently; no power armor plate crafting.

entries.title: POWER ARMOR REPAIRS
entries.notes: Armor plates cannot be crafted. Recover parts from armored enemies, faction dealers or found frames. Repairs use tier-dependent crafting components; higher-tier modules require rarer and more numerous materials, with costs scaling to their damage.

entries.title: POWER ARMOR CONFIGURATION
entries.notes: The six-part condition figure now sits at the center of the service screen. Select any body section, inspect matching armor plates from your backpack, preview durability and protection, then deliberately install, remove, or repair that slot.

entries.title: WEAPON WORKBENCH
entries.notes: Choose an owned weapon, inspect its installed assemblies, select a replacement part, and preview performance and exact material requirements before crafting or installing. Nothing is spent just by inspecting an option.

entries.title: BARTER CONFIRMATION
entries.notes: Adding an item to either side now stages it for a single combined trade. Review everything you are buying and selling, check the net cap balance, and press Confirm Trade once. Closing or clearing the offer exchanges nothing.

entries.title: VENDOR TRADING
entries.notes: Choose exact buy and sell quantities, review live cap totals, sell reserve ammunition, and see your wallet and backpack space beside merchant stock. Sold-out goods, unaffordable offers and equipped gear are clearly marked. Existing merchant prices and saved stock remain intact.

entries.title: LOOT TRANSFERS
entries.notes: Looting now shows container contents beside your backpack, lets you choose stack quantities, reports carry capacity, and clears a case's glow when it is empty. Enemy drops and Take All use the same inventory transfer rules.

entries.title: LOOT CASE GLOW
entries.notes: Loot cases no longer have giant floating LOOT labels. Their physical lids, seams, and latches glow and pulse with a rarity-colored halo. Walk close and press E to search as before.

entries.title: ALWAYS-ON COMPASS
entries.notes: The field compass and power-armor compass remain visible even when no destinations or targets are present. Only combat enemies, active quests, discovered locations, and custom waypoints can create navigation markers; irrelevant NPCs and test landmarks stay off the HUD.

entries.title: QUEST NAVIGATION
entries.notes: Tracked objectives are synchronized with the map and both navigation HUDs. Completed quests are kept in inactive history; empty or inactive objectives no longer leave stray markers.

entries.title: CHARACTER TERMINAL
entries.notes: Status, backpack pages, quest tracking, and the explorable field map are available from the in-game interface.

entries.title: NAVIGATION
entries.notes: Both HUDs now show explored locations and map-set custom waypoints with direction and distance. The weapon workbench uses only the left-hand owned-gun list; its redundant dropdown is gone. Existing merchant stock and equipment systems remain unchanged.

entries.title: DEVELOPER ITEM GRANTS
entries.notes: Admins can open the Developer Panel to search implemented items, grant weapons, armor, ammo and materials, or add caps. Equip granted firearms through I / Backpack. Free crates, resource caches, and cap handouts have been retired from the test field. Normal loot, vendors and quests remain. Visit Station 7 to craft weapon mods with materials you own. Additional release note: Equipment and caps you already owned stay saved. New test saves start with no free guns, ammo reserves or field caches. Developer item grants are limited to signed-in admins; buyers still use actual vendor prices. The map, NPCs, power armor, weapon workbench and quest systems remain available.

entries.title: FAIR ENEMY RADAR
entries.notes: Red dots only reveal enemies after they have spotted you or you have engaged them. Contacts fade shortly after enemies lose sight; undiscovered patrols remain hidden. In power armor, tap E to search nearby enemy drops or crates, or hold E to exit.

entries.title: COMBAT & POWER FRAME
entries.notes: Compact armor silhouette and clearance, deeper rear boarding, softer boot impacts, fusion cores lasting 25% longer, close-quarters enemy tracking, single-render-layer NPCs, concealed enemy tactics, and a bottom red-dot hostile compass.

entries.title: COCKPIT CLEANUP
entries.notes: Removed the two obsolete teal camera-mounted LED strips that followed the player while wearing power armor. The amber gauges and armor-condition figure stay unchanged.

entries.title: ARMOR CONDITION FIGURE
entries.notes: Six independent body segments glow amber when equipped and healthy, red at 30% condition or lower, and dark when destroyed or unequipped. The figure appears at left-middle while wearing the frame.

entries.title: POWER ARMOR INSTRUMENTS
entries.notes: Helmet HUD rebuilt as amber analog gauges: HP and RADS left, a live direction compass centered, and fusion CORE, AP sprint stamina, and stacked AMMO on the right. No large boxes or upper visor overlays. Power-armor visuals, movement and sounds are unchanged.

entries.title: SOUND TIMING
entries.notes: Footsteps use natural walk/sprint cadence, gunshots and impacts have longer decays, and power-armor hydraulics span the full entry animation.

entries.title: REAR ENTRY & SUIT SILHOUETTE
entries.notes: Power armor has deploying rear stairs, an opening central spine, two-joint hip/knee IK, real handle-gripping arms and separate boot contacts. The camera stays outside until the hatch shuts. NPCs must face you before firing; tracers originate at their visible muzzle.
